{{Short description|Type of geometric grid}}
[[Image:Hanan5.svg|thumb|Hanan grid generated for a 5-terminal case]]

In [[geometry]], the '''Hanan grid''' {{math|''H''(''S'')}} of a [[finite set]] {{mvar|S}} of points in [[Plane (geometry)|the plane]] is obtained by constructing vertical and horizontal lines through each point in {{mvar|S}}.

The main motivation for studying the Hanan grid stems from the fact that it is known to contain a minimum length  [[rectilinear Steiner tree]] for {{mvar|S}}.<ref>Martin Zachariasen, ''[http://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/viewdoc/summary?doi=10.1.1.43.3586 A Catalog of Hanan Grid Problems]'' ''Networks'', vol. 38, 2000, pp. 200-221</ref> It is named after Maurice Hanan, who was first<ref>Christine R. Leverenz, 
Miroslaw Truszczynski, [http://portal.acm.org/ft_gateway.cfm?id=306402&type=pdf The Rectilinear Steiner Tree Problem: Algorithms and Examples using Permutations of the Terminal Set], ''1999 ACM Southeast Regional Conference'', 1999, {{doi|10.1145/306363.306402}}</ref> to investigate the rectilinear Steiner minimum tree and introduced this graph.<ref>M. Hanan, [http://amadeus.ecs.umass.edu/mie373/hanan_rsmt.pdf On Steiner's problem with rectilinear distance] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304001742/http://amadeus.ecs.umass.edu/mie373/hanan_rsmt.pdf |date=2016-03-04 }}, J. SIAM Appl. Math. 14 (1966), 255 - 265.</ref>
